spots.name: Palermo Cathedral
spots.summary: Palermo Cathedral is the cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Palermo, located in Palermo, Sicily, southern Italy. It is dedicated to the Assumption of the Virgin Mary.

spots.name: Martorana
spots.summary: The Church of St. Mary of the Admiral, also called Martorana, is the seat of the Parish of San Nicolò dei Greci, overlooking the Piazza Bellini, next to the Norman church of San Cataldo and facing the Baroque church of Santa Caterina, in Palermo, Italy.

spots.name: Palazzo dei Normanni
spots.summary: The Palazzo dei Normanni, also called Royal Palace of Palermo, is a palace in Palermo, Sicily, Italy. It was the seat of the Kings of Sicily with the Hauteville dynasty and served afterwards as the main seat of power for the subsequent rulers of Sicily. Since 1946 it has been the seat of the Sicilian Regional Assembly.

spots.name: Quattro Canti
spots.summary: Quattro Canti, officially known as Piazza Vigliena, is a Baroque square in Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy; it is considered the center of the historic quarters of the city.

spots.name: Cappella Palatina
spots.summary: The Palatine Chapel /ˈpælətaɪn ˈtʃæpəl/ is the royal chapel of the Norman Palace in Palermo, Sicily. This building is a mixture of Byzantine, Norman, and Fatimid architectural styles, showing the tricultural state of Sicily during the 12th century after Roger I and Robert Guiscard conquered the island.

spots.name: Church of San Cataldo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of San Cataldo is a Catholic church located at Piazza Bellini, in central Palermo, Sicily, Italy. Erected in 1154 as a notable example of the Arab-Norman architecture which flourished in Sicily under Norman rule on the island, the church is annexed to that of Santa Maria dell'Ammiraglio.

spots.name: Piazza Pretoria
spots.summary: Piazza Pretoria is at the limits of the district of Kalsa, near the corner of Cassaro with Via Maqueda, just a few meters from the Quattro Canti, the intersection where all the four ancient quarters intersect, in the city of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Santa Caterina, Palermo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Caterina d'Alessandria or Saint Catherine of Alexandria is a Roman Catholic church with a main facade on Piazza Bellini, and a lateral Western facade facing the elaborate Fontana Pretoria, in the historic quarter of Kalsa in the city of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Fontana Pretoria
spots.summary: The Praetorian Fountain is a monumental fountain located in Piazza Pretoria in the historic center of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy. The fountain dominates the piazza on the west flank of the church of Santa Caterina, and is one block south of the intersection of the Quattro Canti.

spots.name: Teatro Massimo

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Teatro Massimo Vittorio Emanuele is an opera house and opera company located on the Piazza Verdi in Palermo, Sicily. It was dedicated to King Victor Emanuel II. It is the biggest in Italy, and one of the largest of Europe, renowned for its perfect acoustics.

spots.name: Arab-Norman Palermo and the Cathedral Churches of Cefalù and Monreale
spots.summary: The Arab-Norman Palermo and the Cathedral Churches of Cefalù and Monreale are a series of nine religious and civic structures located on the northern coast of Sicily dating from the era of the Norman Kingdom of Sicily (1130-1194): two palaces, three churches, a cathedral, and a bridge in Palermo, as well as the cathedrals of Cefalù and Monreale.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Arab-Norman Palermo and the Cathedral Churches of Cefalù and Monreale

spots.name: Church of the Gesù

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Gesù, known also as the Saint Mary of Jesus or the Casa Professa, is a Baroque-style, Roman Catholic church established under the patronage of the Jesuit order, and located at Piazza Casa Professa 21 in Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: San Giuseppe dei Teatini

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Giuseppe dei Teatini is a Roman Catholic church on Via Vittorio Emanuele, at the southwest corner of the Quattro Canti, in the historic center of the city of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy. The east flank of the nave faces the Fontana Pretoria, across the piazza from Santa Caterina.

spots.name: Porta Nuova
spots.summary: Porta Nuova is a monumental city gate of Palermo. It represents the entrance of the Cassaro from Corso Calatafimi and is located beside Palazzo dei Normanni, royal palace of Palermo. The gate was built to celebrate Charles V's conquest of Tunis (1535) and his visit to the capital of the Kingdom of Sicily.

spots.name: Via Maqueda
spots.summary: Via Maqueda, also known as Strada Nuova, is an important street of Palermo, Sicily. Together with the Cassaro, it represents the main axis of the historic centre and provides access to a number of important sights, including Teatro Massimo and Fontana Pretoria.

spots.name: San Giovanni degli Eremiti

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: San Giovanni degli Eremiti is an ancient former monastic church located on Via Benedettini #19 in the ancient quarter of Albergaria of the city of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy. It is about two blocks south from the Palazzo dei Normanni, adjacent to the church of San Giorgio in Kemonia.

spots.name: Cassaro, Palermo
spots.summary: The Cassaro is the most ancient street of Palermo. From the late 16th century the street also had the name Via Toledo. Following the unification of Italy, it was officially renamed Via Vittorio Emanuele II, but the old and distinctive name is still in use.

spots.name: Palazzo Chiaramonte

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Palazzo Chiaramonte-Steri is a 14th-century palace in Palermo, Sicily. Built for the powerful Chiaramonte family, it later served as the residence of the viceroys of Sicily and, from 1604 to 1782, as the seat of the Inquisition in Palermo; since 1943 it has housed the rectorate of the University of Palermo.

spots.name: San Domenico, Palermo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Domenico is a Baroque-style Roman Catholic church, located on Piazza San Domenico, and located in the ancient quarter of La Loggia, in central Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Palazzo Pretorio

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Praetorian Palace, also known as Palace of the Eagles, is a palace of Palermo. The building has an important role in the political life of the city, since it houses the mayor and the offices of the municipality of Palermo.

spots.name: Palazzo Abatellis

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Palazzo Abatellis is a palazzo in Palermo, Sicily, southern Italy, located in the Kalsa quarter. It is home to the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, the Gallery of Art for the Sicilian region.

spots.name: Zisa, Palermo
spots.summary: The Zisa is a grand 12th-century Norman hunting lodge and summer palace in the western area of Palermo, in the region of Sicily, Italy. The edifice was started around 1165 by Arab craftsmen under the rule of the Norman conqueror of Sicily, king William I. It was not finished until 1189, under the rule of William II.

spots.name: Teatro Politeama
spots.summary: The Politeama Theatre, complete name Teatro Politeama Garibaldi is a theatre of Palermo. It is located in the central Piazza Ruggero Settimo and represents the second most important theatre of the city after the Teatro Massimo. It houses the Orchestra Sinfonica Siciliana.

spots.name: Villino Florio

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Villino Florio is a private residence designed in an eclectic Art Nouveau (Liberty) style by Ernesto Basile, and located on Viale Regina Margherita #38 in the city of Palermo, Siciy, Italy.

spots.name: Orto botanico di Palermo
spots.summary: The Orto Botanico di Palermo is both a botanical garden and a research and educational institution of the Department of Botany of the University of Palermo. The garden lies within the city of Palermo, Italy at 10 m (33 ft) above sea-level.

spots.name: Piazza Bellini, Palermo
spots.summary: Piazza Bellini is a square of Palermo. It is located in the heart of the city, near the central Via Maqueda and Piazza Pretoria, in the quarter of the Kalsa, within the historic centre of Palermo.

spots.name: Santa Maria dello Spasimo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Maria dello Spasimo, or Lo Spasimo, is an unfinished Catholic church in the Kalsa neighborhood in Palermo, Sicily, on Via dello Spasimo.

spots.name: Palazzina Cinese

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chinese Palace, also known as Real Casina alla Cinese, is a former royal residence of the House of Bourbon-Two Sicilies designed in the style of Chinoiserie. It is located in Palermo, inside the park of La Favorita.

spots.name: Cuba Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cuba is a recreational palace in the Sicilian city of Palermo, originally part of the Sollazzi Regi group of Norman palaces. It was built in 1180 by William II of Sicily in his Royal Park, together with an artificial lake. The name Cuba derives either from its cubical form, or the Arabic Qubba, "dome".

spots.name: Admiral's bridge
spots.summary: The Admiral's Bridge is a medieval bridge of Palermo, located in Piazza Scaffa. It was built over the Oreto River during the era of the Norman Sicily by the ammiratus ammiratorum George of Antioch.

spots.name: Santissimo Salvatore, Palermo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Most Holy Saviour is a Baroque-style, Roman Catholic church in Palermo, Italy. It is located at #396 of the ancient main street of Palermo, the Cassaro, presently Via Vittorio Emanuele, in the ancient Albergaria quarter.

spots.name: Villa Giulia
spots.summary: The Villa Giulia, also known as Villa del Popolo, and as Villa Flor is an urban public park, lying to the east of the Botanical Garden of Palermo, in the region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: San Matteo al Cassaro

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of San Matteo al Cassaro is a Baroque-style, Roman Catholic church of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy. It is located in the main street of the city, the ancient Cassaro now Corso Vittorio Emanuele, in the quarter of the Loggia, about a block east of the Quattro Canti, within the historic centre of Palermo.

spots.name: Piazza Marina
spots.summary: Piazza Marina is a square of Palermo. It is located down the Cassaro street, in the quarter of the Kalsa, within the historic centre of Palermo. The square is dominated by the great Garibaldi Garden.

spots.name: Antonino Salinas Regional Archaeological Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Antonino Salinas Regional Archeological Museum is a museum in Palermo, Italy. It possesses one of the richest collections of Punic and Ancient Greek art in Italy, as well as many items related to the history of Sicily.

spots.name: Palazzo Valguarnera-Gangi

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palazzo Valguarnera-Gangi is an urban palace, first of the Princes Valguarnera and then of the Princes Gangi, situated in the Piazza Croce dei Vespri, in the ancient quarter of the Kalsa in the city of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Santa Maria della Catena

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Maria della Catena is a Roman Catholic church located in the Piazza Dogana, now sandwiched between Strada Statale 113 and Via Vittorio Emanuele, located in the harbor-hugging quarter of Castellammare in Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Oratorio del Rosario di Santa Cita

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Oratorio del Rosario di Santa Cita is a Baroque prayer room or oratory located in the quarter of the Castellammare within the historic center of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy. The site is best known for the remarkable stucco tableaux scenes composed during 1687-1718 by Giacomo Serpotta.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Oratorio del Rosario di Santa Cita, Palermo

spots.name: Santa Maria della Pietà, Palermo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Mary of Pity is a Baroque church of Palermo. It is located at the corner of Via Alloro and Via Torremuzza in the quarter of the Kalsa, within the historic centre of Palermo.

spots.name: Porta Felice
spots.summary: Porta Felice is a monumental city gate of Palermo, Sicily; the gate is located in the zone of the Foro Italico and the Castellammare quarter. It represents the water-side entrance into Via Vittorio Emanuele, the most ancient main street of the city.

spots.name: Castello a Mare

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Castello a Mare or Castellammare is an ancient fortress that guarded the entrance to the port at Palermo in La Cala. Extensive remains are visible, some of which are open to the public. There is a Norman keep, a fortified gate or entrance, and remains of a sophisticated Renaissance star-shaped defence.

spots.name: Santa Ninfa dei Crociferi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Nympha is a Baroque-Mannerist church of Palermo. The facade rises on Via Maqueda, a block north of the central intersection known as the Quattro Canti, in the quarter of Seralcadi, within the historic centre of Palermo. The church belongs to the Camillians.

spots.name: Palazzo Butera

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Butera is a Baroque-style aristocratic palace located facing the Mediterranean in the ancient quarter of Kalsa of central Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Oratory of San Lorenzo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Oratory of Saint Lawrence is a Baroque oratory of Palermo. It is located near the Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi, in the quarter of the Kalsa, within the historic centre of Palermo.

spots.name: Villa Malfitano Whitaker

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Villa Malfitano Whitaker is a 19th-century villa in Via Dante, in the quarter of Politeama of Palermo, Sicily. It is presently a museum displaying Whitaker's natural history and archaeological collections, as well as his artwork.

spots.name: Palazzo Alliata di Villafranca

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Alliata di Villafranca is former aristocratic palace, now converted into a museum, located just off Via Vittorio Emanuele facing the Piazza Bologni which opens two blocks west of the Quattro Canti intersection, in the ancient quarter of the Albergaria of the city of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Palazzo Riso

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Palazzo Riso, officially RISO, Museo d'Arte Contemporanea della Sicilia and also known as Palazzo Belmonte Riso, is a regional contemporary art museum located in the ancient Corso Vittorio Emanuele, Palermo, Italy.

spots.name: Santa Maria della Gancia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Maria della Gancia, also known as Santa Maria degli Angeli, is a 15th-century Roman Catholic church, adjacent to a convent, located on Via Alloro #27 in central Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Piazza Castelnuovo
spots.summary: Piazza Castelnuovo is a square of Palermo. Along with the contiguous Piazza Ruggero Settimo, it forms a single urban space, commonly called Piazza Politeama, by virtue of the presence of Teatro Politeama, the second most important theatre of the city after Teatro Massimo.

spots.name: Bonocore Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Bonocore is a Neoclassical palace located on the north side of Piazza Pretoria in central Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Giardino Inglese
spots.summary: The Piersanti Mattarella Park, formerly the English Garden, is a public park in Palermo designed in 1851 by the architect Giovan Battista Filippo Basile.

spots.name: Santa Teresa alla Kalsa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Teresa is a Baroque Roman Catholic church, located on Piazza della Kalsa, facing the Porta de Greci in the ancient quarter of the Kalsa of the city of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Immacolata Concezione al Capo

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Church of the Immaculate Conception is a Baroque church of Palermo. It is located on the busy streets composing the markets of the Capo, in the quarter of the Seralcadio, within the historic centre of Palermo.

spots.name: Palazzo Branciforte

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Branciforte is Renaissance-style aristocratic palace located on Via Bara dell'Olivella, in the historic center of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy.

spots.name: Piazza Verdi, Palermo
spots.summary: Piazza Verdi, commonly known as Piazza Massimo, is a square of Palermo. At its centre is the sumptuous Teatro Massimo, the biggest opera house of Italy, and the third of Europe after the Opéra National de Paris and the K. K. Hof-Opernhaus in Vienna.

Palermo Botanical Garden
spots.summary: Historical city botanical gardens featuring many collections of plants, trees, and aquaculture. The garden is associated with the neighbouring university and contains a number of experimental gardens to test acclimation of plant species to Sicily.

spots.summary: Bistro in the centre of Palermo with a wide choice of vegetarian and vegan dishes. Beautiful restaurant, with retro air, very unique old bookstore. Smiling waitress, very good food, decent waiting time.

spots.summary: This location has a certain charm, with a quite rare calm in Palermo. The service is impeccable. The vegetarian menu was really good. Delicious wines and fantastic food!

spots.name: Maqueda Bistrot

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site
